name: Minotaur (Far Distant Future Publishing)
body:
According to many accounts, their current form was thrust upon the minotaurs as a divine curse, punishment for their obstinance and disobedience. Many minotaurs tell the story differently, reporting that they were transformed into bull-people as a reward by a deity that saw their true potential.

Appearance

Minotaurs are tall, powerfully muscled humanoids. Their upper bodies are human-looking, but they have the heads and legs of bulls, and their shoulders and lower bodies are covered in thick fur. Minotaurs of both sexes have immense bull heads characterized by fierce red eyes and sharp, forward-facing horns.

While some minotaurs prefer a wild, unkept appearance, many take pride in adorning themselves with armor, bracers, and jewelry.

Nose rings and adornments on their horns are considered especially prestigious status symbols.

Social

Most minotaurs are solitary creatures. They will sometimes work for or with others, but they like boundaries and they insist on being in control of their own environment. Minotaurs rarely congregate in large numbers. Minotaurs are naturally drawn to mazes; while not known for their great intelligence, their minds are exceptionally gifted when it comes to orienteering and solving puzzles. They prefer to lure opponents into environments that confuse, befuddle, and frustrate them, while giving themselves the upper hand with their superior spatial awareness. While they do not usually gather in large numbers, minotaur communities are not unheard of, and they also sometimes integrate into communities of humans or other humanoids. The larger the settlement, the more complex the politics become, as minotaurs put their puzzle-solving prowess to work weaving labyrinthine networks of interpersonal relationships.

Alignment and Religion

Minotaurs tend to be obsessive, and have little time for anyone’s priorities other than their own. The typical minotaur is selfish and standoffish, distrustful of strangers and of society as a whole. As a result, minotaurs tend toward both Chaotic and Evil alignments. However, those who are more comfortable around interpersonal politics may be Lawful instead, as they subtly try to control those around them.

Traditionally, most minotaurs worship Baphomet, a demon lord who appears as a great minotaur. Few are devout, giving only lip service to Baphomet, although his cult does loom large over minotaur society.

Minotaurs are notoriously self-willed, though, and many have their own ideas about faith-some venerating other demon lords, and others engaging in more personal journeys of religious enlightenment.

Names

Some typical minotaur names include the following (choose or roll 1d12): 1 Antipatha, 2 Asterion, 3 Berredevilo, 4 Deleazeva, 5 Epignikios, 6 Kataramio, 7 Lavyrele, 8 Monakirros, 9 Oria, 10 Pelachio, 11 Synkrichios, 12 Xyskrinthio

Common Traits
Ability Score Modifiers You are sturdy and strong, but dull and disagreeable. Your ability score modifiers are +2 Str, +2 Con, -2 Cha [specialized]. (1)
Size As a Medium creature, you have no bonuses or penalties due to size. (0)
Type You are a Monstrous Humanoid. (3)
Speed Your base speed is 30 feet. (0)
Languages You begin play speaking Common and Giant. If you have a high Intelligence score, you can choose from any of the following languages: Draconic, Dwarven, Sylvan, and Undercommon. (0)
Other Traits
Darkvision You have darkvision 60 feet. (-)
Horns You can make a gore attack with your horns. This is a primary natural attack that deals 1d4 piercing damage for a Medium minotaur (1d6 if Large). (1)
Natural Armor Your tough, resilient hide provides a +1 natural armor bonus to AC. (2)
Natural Cunning You are immune to flanking. In addition, you gain a +4 species bonus to Survival checks to avoid getting lost, and you can use know direction at will as a spell-like ability, using your character level as the caster level. (4)
Powerful Charge Whenever you charge, you deal double your normal damage dice with your gore natural attack plus 1-1/2 times your Strength bonus. (2)
Total: 13 RP (advanced)
Minotaur Variant
Large Minotaur (19 RP)

While the largest number of minotaurs are Medium, the most dangerous specimens are those who seem to be the most strongly affected by the species’ curse. These individuals grow larger but also have minds even more clouded by hatred and obsession. You are size Large, and your reach is 10 feet. Your net ability score modifiers (including the adjustments for being size Large) are +4 Str, +2 Con, -2 Dex, -2 Int, -4 Cha. This alters your size and ability scores.

Alternate Traits
Bully You gain a +2 species bonus to bull rush attempts, and a +2 species bonus to Intimidate checks. This trait replaces natural cunning.
Labyrinth Magic You cast any spell with “confusion” or “maze” in its name at +1 caster level. This trait replaces powerful charge.
Mechanical You gain a +2 species bonus to Craft (traps) checks. You also gain proficiency with double crossbows and a +1 species bonus to attack rolls with all crossbows. This trait replaces natural cunning.
Silver Tongued You gain a +2 bonus on Diplomacy and Bluff checks. In addition, when you use Diplomacy to shift a creature’s attitude, you can do so up to three steps up rather than just two. This trait replaces natural cunning.
Stubborn You gain a +2 species bonus on Will saving throws to resist spells and spell-like abilities of the enchantment (charm) and enchantment (compulsion) subschools. In addition, if you fail such a save, you receive another save 1 round later to prematurely end the effect (assuming the spell or spell-like ability has a duration greater than 1 round). This second save is made at the same DC as the first. If you have a similar ability from another source (such as a rogue‘s slippery mind class feature), you can only use one of these abilities per round, but can try the other on the second round if the first reroll ability fails. This trait replaces natural armor.
Tremorsense You gain tremorsense with a range of 30 feet. This trait replaces darkvision.
Favored Class Bonuses
Barbarian Add +1 to your total number of rage rounds per day.
Brawler Add +1 to your CMD when resisting a bull rush or grapple attempt.
Cleric Select one domain power granted at 1st level that is normally usable a number of times per day equal to 3 + your Wisdom modifier. Add +1/2 to the number of uses per day of that domain power.
Fighter Add +1 to your CMD when resisting a bull rush or reposition attempt.
Monk Add a +1/4 bonus on combat maneuver checks made to bull rush or grapple.
Oracle Add +1 spell known from the oracle spell list. This spell must be at least one spell level below the highest-level oracle spell you can cast.
Ranger Choose a weapon from the following list: gore, bastard sword, glaive, greataxe, or any type of crossbow. Add +1/2 on critical hit confirmation rolls made while using that weapon (maximum bonus of +4). This bonus does not stack with Critical Focus.
Rogue Reduce the penalty for not being proficient with one weapon by 1. When the nonproficiency penalty for a weapon becomes 0 because of this ability, you are treated as having the appropriate Martial or Exotic Weapon Proficiency feat with that weapon.
Witch Add +1/6 of a new witch hex.

Awesome Ancestries: Fantasy Animal Humanoids, Vol. 3 - Born to Be Wild. © 2025, Far Distant Future Publishing; Author: Bryan Mangum.
